newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saudis urged to do more on market access at WTO.
newsitem.headline: Saudis urged to do more on market access at WTO.

text.p: Trade diplomats reported progress on Thursday in Saudi Arabia's third round of talks on joining the World Trade Organisation but urged the kingdom to do more to present detailed offers on market access.
A WTO spokesman said Saudi Arabia was asked to present offers in areas of import licences, agriculture, customs valuation and technical barriers to trade on the first day of the two-day talks.
Commerce Minister Osamah bin Jaafar bin Ibrahim Faqih led the delegation in the WTO accession working party negotiating the terms of entry to the 131-member trade body.

The latest round of talks are the third since the world's largest oil producer applied in July 1993 to join the trade watchdog's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). The first WTO round was held in May 1996.
Saudi Arabia is eager to diversify its heavily oil-dependent economy and has hinted it wants to join on the favourable terms granted to developing countries.
Trade diplomats said the next meeting was unlikely before October or November even if Saudi Arabia presented its offers by September to its trading partners which must then study them.

Concerns among the trading partners include Saudi Arabia's restrictions on import licensing in areas such as chemicals and pasteurised milk, information technology products, agricultural equipment and machinery as well as the scope of its curbs.
